items.title: Mail Management System
items.description: A production document-routing and approval platform for the Department of Agrarian Development, combining multi-level workflows, secure private document handling, audit trails, and controlled OpenShift releases.

details.overview: A production document-routing and approval platform developed for the Department of Agrarian Development to manage official correspondence across departments and divisions. The system supports multi-level approval workflows, document distribution and tracking, minute notes, organizational hierarchies, granular permission-based access control, private document storage, audit trails, dashboards, and administrative workflows.
highlights: Developed full-stack application and database components using PHP and MySQL for document creation, distribution, approval, tracking, search, and administrative workflows.
Implemented role- and permission-based access controls, multi-level approval processes, comprehensive audit trails, private document handling, and Redis-backed application sessions.
Migrated the frontend runtime from VM-based deployment to a native Red Hat OpenShift architecture using Deployments, Services, Routes, ConfigMaps, Secrets, persistent volumes, and Kustomize.
Adapted the application container to operate as a non-root workload under OpenShift restricted security constraints.
Built a CI/CD release path using GitHub Actions, private GHCR container images, immutable image digests, and controlled OpenShift production deployment.
Developed production promotion and rollback tooling with release identity verification, health checks, persistent-storage validation, and post-deployment verification.
Performed production-candidate validation covering authentication, document access, uploads/downloads, persistent storage, database connectivity, Redis connectivity, readiness, and liveness.

architecture.deployment: Production architecture on Red Hat OpenShift with private document storage and Redis-backed sessions.

items.title: Nextcloud on OpenShift
items.category: Private Cloud / Security / OpenShift / MCP Integration
items.description: A private cloud file platform deployed natively on Red Hat OpenShift with persistent storage, dedicated PostgreSQL and Redis services, restricted container security, and a private MCP integration under controlled OAuth validation.

details.overview: A separate native OpenShift Nextcloud deployment for the Department of Agrarian Development, designed for private file storage and a private MCP integration for ChatGPT. The stable application baseline combines PHP-FPM and Nginx, persistent file and database storage, dedicated PostgreSQL, and authenticated Redis. Multi-user MCP and OAuth integration remain under controlled validation, with end-to-end account linking and user isolation still pending.
highlights: Deployed Nextcloud as a native OpenShift workload using PHP-FPM and Nginx, dedicated PostgreSQL, authenticated Redis, and persistent volume claims.
Adapted workloads to OpenShift restricted-v2 security with arbitrary runtime UIDs and no fixed-UID exception.
Kept database, cache, and MCP services private inside the cluster while exposing only Nextcloud through a public Route.
Established a private five-tool MCP baseline for file operations through Nextcloud WebDAV and OCS APIs using a dedicated non-admin account.
Developed a multi-user MCP runtime that uses verified OAuth identity and dedicated PostgreSQL persistence, with app-password material encrypted using AES-256-GCM.
Deployed a secure MCP tunnel runtime with an immutable image digest, read-only root filesystem, disabled service-account token automount, and health checks.
Validated restricted workload startup, readiness, rollout stability, and unauthenticated HTTP 401 responses; real ChatGPT OAuth and multi-user isolation remain under controlled validation.

architecture.alt: Nextcloud on OpenShift system architecture diagram
architecture.deployment: Native OpenShift file storage with private PostgreSQL, Redis, and MCP services; multi-user OAuth integration under controlled validation.
